scaffold.description: Value stream scaffold for Buildcraft, a home improvement and building materials retailer. Covers the Customer Engagement and Fulfillment cluster: Multi-Channel Journeys (B2C omnichannel), In-Store Sales (expert-led retail), and Creating Frame Agreements (B2B contractor).
scaffold.industry: Retail — Home Improvement and Building Materials

vs_multi_channel.name: Multi-Channel Journeys
vs_multi_channel.description: Delivers a seamless shopping experience across online, mobile, and in-store channels — from initial product discovery through to order fulfillment.

vs_in_store_sales.name: In-Store Sales
vs_in_store_sales.description: Delivers expert-assisted sales and design advisory within the physical store environment, from customer greeting through to transaction and fulfillment arrangement.

vs_frame_agreements.name: Creating Frame Agreements
vs_frame_agreements.description: Establishes structured commercial agreements with contractor and construction company accounts, enabling volume purchasing, preferred pricing, and long-term retention.

act_mcj_01.name: Initiate Channel Session
act_mcj_01.description: Customer enters a shopping channel — website, app, or store — and a session is established. Channel identity is captured for continuity.

act_mcj_02.name: Discover and Browse Products
act_mcj_02.description: Customer browses catalogue, uses search, or receives AI-driven recommendations. Personalisation engine surfaces relevant products based on profile and behaviour.

act_mcj_03.name: Add to Cart
act_mcj_03.description: Customer selects product(s) and adds to cart. Stock availability is checked in real-time. Cart persists across channels via unified customer profile.

act_mcj_04.name: Initiate Checkout
act_mcj_04.description: Customer proceeds to checkout. Identity is confirmed, delivery/collection preference is captured, and payment method is selected.

act_mcj_05.name: Process Payment and Confirm Order
act_mcj_05.description: Payment is processed via POS or online gateway. Order record is created, confirmation is issued to customer, and downstream fulfillment is triggered.

act_mcj_06.name: Allocate Fulfillment Channel
act_mcj_06.description: Order is routed to appropriate fulfillment method: home delivery, click-and-collect, or in-store pickup. SLA commitment is set based on product category and location.

act_mcj_07.name: Deliver or Make Available for Collection
act_mcj_07.description: Order is physically delivered to customer or made ready for collection. Tracking information is provided. Completion is confirmed via customer acknowledgement.

activities: Deliver or Make Available for Collection

act_iss_01.name: Welcome and Assess Customer Need
act_iss_01.description: Store associate greets customer and determines the nature of purchase — simple product selection vs. complex project requiring advisory.

act_iss_02.name: Guide Product Selection or Design
act_iss_02.description: For simple purchases, associate guides to product location. For complex projects (e.g. kitchen fit-out), design consultant engages to scope a solution using planning tools.

act_iss_03.name: Process In-Store Transaction
act_iss_03.description: Customer proceeds to POS. Transaction is processed. Loyalty program is applied if applicable. Receipt and any warranty documentation is issued.

act_iss_04.name: Arrange Fulfillment for Store Sale
act_iss_04.description: For items not carried in store or requiring delivery, order is passed to fulfillment coordinator. Click-and-collect or delivery SLA is committed.

act_cfa_01.name: Identify and Qualify Contractor Account
act_cfa_01.description: Account manager identifies prospective contractor or construction company. Account is qualified against volume potential, creditworthiness, and strategic fit.

act_cfa_02.name: Negotiate Pricing and Volume Terms
act_cfa_02.description: Account manager and contractor negotiate bulk pricing tiers, volume commitments, product categories, and agreement duration. Pricing policy approval is obtained for non-standard terms.

act_cfa_03.name: Execute Frame Agreement
act_cfa_03.description: Agreement is formalised, signed by both parties, and entered into the commercial system. Credit limit is set. Account is flagged for contractor pricing.

act_cfa_04.name: Onboard Contractor Account
act_cfa_04.description: Contractor account is set up in CRM and ordering systems. Dedicated account portal access is provisioned. Bulk order process is communicated and confirmed.

scaffold.name: Buildcraft — Customer Engagement and Fulfillment

observations.rationale: High cart abandonment (45% current vs 30% target) is driven by legacy checkout system causing performance failures and payment errors. Customers abandon at the payment step rather than from purchase intent change.

evidence.excerpt: Cart Abandonment Rate 45% vs 30% target (Objectives_Key_Results). Pain point: 'Legacy checkout system causing performance and payment failures' (High urgency, Immediate).

observations.rationale: CRM data is fragmented across online and in-store systems following a failed GDPR implementation. Customer profiles are incomplete (75% vs 95% target), preventing personalised recommendations and cross-channel continuity.

evidence.excerpt: Customer profile completeness 75% vs 95% target. Pain points: 'Broken CRM data due to failed GDPR implementation' (High, Immediate) and 'Customer data fragmentation preventing personalized engagement' (High, Short-Term).

observations.rationale: Current delivery lead time of 5 days is significantly behind competitor next-day delivery capability. Fulfillment channel allocation is partially manual, creating routing delays particularly for high-demand SKUs.

evidence.excerpt: Delivery Lead Time 5 days vs 2 day target. Competitor pain point: 'Competitors offer next-day delivery; we take 5 days' (High, Immediate, Behind). Pain point: 'Competitors use automated order fulfillment; our process is partially manual' (High, Short-Term).

observations.rationale: Discount and promotional pricing decisions are made independently across in-store, online, and B2B channels with no unified pricing authority. This creates inconsistent customer experiences and margin leakage when customers cross channels to exploit pricing differences.

evidence.excerpt: Pricing Policy governs three separate activities across two VS without unified governance. Pain point: 'Competitor pricing algorithms personalize discounts dynamically; we use static pricing' (High, Short-Term, Behind). Gross Margin target 45% vs 40% current.

observations.rationale: New sustainability regulations are creating compliance obligations across product selection, supplier onboarding, and order documentation. Compliance gatekeeping has not been integrated into existing operational flows, creating ad-hoc review overhead.

evidence.excerpt: Pain point: 'New sustainability regulations increasing compliance complexity' (Medium, Long-Term, High resolution complexity). Business Outcome: 'Order Documents Display Circular Products for Transparency' (Positioning theme).

bindingConstraint.justification: Fragmented pricing authority is the single governing constraint that spans all three value streams simultaneously. It creates inconsistent customer experiences across channels (fo_003), prevents dynamic discount capability that competitors use to drive conversion (fo_001), and slows B2B agreement execution where non-standard pricing requires multi-step approval (fo_007). Unlike execution friction (checkout system, delivery lead time) which can be fixed independently per stream, pricing authority fragmentation requires a structural governance change affecting all three streams at once — making it the binding constraint on enterprise-wide conversion improvement.

observations.rationale: Cart contents, customer history, and recommendations do not carry across channels. Customers who browse online and purchase in-store (or vice versa) encounter a broken experience, reducing conversion and NPS.

evidence.excerpt: Omnichannel NPS 45 vs 60 target. Pain point: 'No integration between online and in-store experiences' (Medium, Short-Term). Competitor pain point: 'Competitors provide an integrated omnichannel shopping experience; our online and in-store experience is disconnected' (High, Behind).

observations.rationale: Customers planning complex projects (kitchens, bathrooms, renovations) cannot complete planning digitally — they must attend store. Design advisory capability is not available online, creating a channel bottleneck at in-store design consultation.

evidence.excerpt: Pain point: 'Customers struggle with complex purchases (e.g., kitchens)' (High, Short-Term). Customer Journey: 'Planning and Building a Kitchen' — NPS High, Lead Time Long. Strategy: 'Own the DIY Planning Journey' (2025).

bindingConstraint.justification: Primary constraint identified within vs_in_store_sales value stream.

observations.rationale: Frame agreement onboarding and ordering process is manual and slow. Contractor accounts lack a self-service portal. B2B bulk ordering relies on account manager coordination rather than system-enabled automation.

evidence.excerpt: Pain point: 'B2B bulk ordering process is inefficient for contractors' (Medium, Short-Term). Bulk Order Volume Growth currently 0% vs 20% YoY target. Strategy: 'Strengthen B2B Engagement and Retention' (2025, High complexity).

observations.rationale: Commercial credit approval for frame agreements is concentrated in a single Credit Controller role. Non-standard pricing terms and credit limit exceptions require sequential approval, extending agreement execution time and creating a decision bottleneck.

evidence.excerpt: Commercial Credit Policy requires single-role approval for all B2B credit. Frame agreement execution involves both pricing and credit approval with no parallel processing. Contractor repeat purchase rate 40% vs 55% target — onboarding friction contributes to early churn.

bindingConstraint.justification: Primary constraint identified within vs_frame_agreements value stream.
